costGuide.title: MG 15S4C Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a 15S4C typically takes 6-8 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes. [PATTERN DATA - based on typical 4-cylinder transverse petrol engine labour]
paragraphs: (All figures . Fitted = supply price + labour band below.)

What genuinely moves the 15S4C replacement price is the engine's age and revision - early units (2011-2015) had timing chain tensioner concerns that later revisions addressed. A used unit from a 2018+ ZS will typically command a higher price than a 2013 MG3 unit due to lower mileage and improved tensioner design. The presence of a documented timing chain replacement adds significant value to any used 15S4C. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: MG 15S4C Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing chain tensioner wear - 60k-100k miles (early units)
items.whatHappens: The 15S4C uses a chain-driven timing system. On the earliest production units (2011-2015), the chain tensioner showed premature wear, leading to chain slack and, in some reported cases, chain breakage without audible warning. Once the chain breaks, the engine is typically beyond economical repair - valve/piston contact is almost guaranteed, and the block rarely survives intact. Later revisions (2015 onwards) received improved tensioner design.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early (rattle on cold start, before failure), chain and tensioner replacement is the economical route - budget £500-£1,000 for the job. If the chain has already failed, the engine is almost certainly scrap - full replacement is the only viable option.

items.title: Oil consumption - higher-mileage units
items.whatHappens: Some higher-mileage 15S4C engines develop increased oil consumption due to piston ring wear. This is not a universal problem but is reported more frequently on engines that have had extended oil service intervals. Consumption of 1 litre per 1,000 miles is a warning sign.
items.repairVsReplace: Piston ring replacement is a significant strip-down job - typically £1,500-£2,500 at a specialist. For most owners, the cost approaches the value of a used replacement engine, making a straight swap the more economical choice.

items.title: EGR carbon buildup
items.whatHappens: Like many modern petrol engines, the 15S4C can suffer from carbon buildup in the EGR system, particularly on cars used predominantly for short urban trips. This can cause rough idling, hesitation, and in some cases, stalling.
items.repairVsReplace: EGR cleaning or replacement is a straightforward job - budget £200-£400 at an independent specialist. This is rarely an engine-replacement trigger on its own.

failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2015 15S4C units received improved timing chain tensioner design; the issue is far less reported after that change. The 15S4C is considered a generally reliable, durable engine when properly maintained.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 15S4C
variants.intro: The 15S4C is one of several 15S-family codes used by SAIC/MG. Later revisions - 15S4E (2018-2023) and 15S4F (2023+) - exist, and while they share the same basic architecture, they have different tuning and emissions calibrations. Where to find the code: The engine code is stamped on the engine block, typically on the front or side of the block near the timing cover. It also appears on the V5C registration document under "Engine number" (the first characters of the engine number). Alternatively, a VIN decoder will confirm the exact factory build code. Which codes get confused with it: The 15S4C is frequently confused with the later 15S4E (2018-2023) and 15S4F (2023+) revisions. While visually similar and physically interchangeable in many cases, ECU calibrations and emissions equipment differ. The [15S4E] and [15S4F] cover those revisions. The 15S4C is also related to the 15S4U (109 hp variant) used in some Roewe models. Why fitting the wrong revision matters: A later 15S4E or 15S4F may physically bolt in but can cause ECU compatibility issues, incorrect fuel mapping, or emissions test failures. Always match the exact suffix when buying a replacement 15S4C, or be prepared to swap the ECU and wiring loom.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 15S4C - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used 15S4C makes sense for low-value MG3s (sub-£3,000 examples) where a recon investment doesn't stack up. The key risk is timing chain history - early 15S4C units (pre-2015) without documented chain replacement are risky. Only buy with compression test results and a clear history. Post-2015 units are generally safer bets.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: The recommended route for most 15S4C replacements. A proper recon addresses the timing chain and tensioner (the primary failure point), replaces piston rings if wear is detected, and includes new gaskets and seals throughout. For a £1,200-£2,200 investment, you get a 12-24 month warranty and an engine that should be good for another 80k+ miles. This is the sensible choice for MG ZS owners where the vehicle value justifies the spend.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full 15S4C rebuild is generally only justified for low-mileage, numbers-matching cars or where the block itself is in exceptional condition. Typical costs £2,000-£3,200. For most owners, reconditioned is the smarter and more cost-effective choice.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All our vetted specialists offer supply-only, supply-and-fit, or full workshop installation. Fitting through the network includes a 12-month warranty on parts and labour, with nationwide delivery to your chosen garage or home address.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The 15S4C is found across MG models with varying values. For an early MG3 worth £1,500-£4,000, a £1,200+ recon may be borderline - consider a used unit or evaluate scrap value first. For MG ZS hosts in the £6,000-£14,000 bracket, a reconditioned 15S4C is financially viable and often the most sensible decision. Always compare the lowest viable replacement cost against your car's current market value - if the engine repair exceeds 60% of the vehicle's worth, scrapping may be the better outcome.

items.question: How much does an MG 15S4C engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned 15S4C typically costs £1,200-£2,200 supply-only, with fitted prices ranging from £1,590-£2,920 depending on labour and warranty. Used units are cheaper at £400-£900 supply-only but carry higher risk. A full rebuild can exceed £3,200 if the block requires extensive machining. Always factor in fitting time (6-8 hours) at local indie rates.

items.question: What is the most common failure on the 15S4C?
items.answer: The most widely reported issue is premature timing chain tensioner wear, particularly on early 2011-2015 units, which can lead to chain breakage and catastrophic engine failure if not addressed. Cold-start rattle is the primary early warning sign. Post-2015 engines received an improved tensioner design. Preventative chain replacement costs £500-£1,000; failure typically writes off the engine.
bullets: Cold-start rattle is the primary early warning sign.

items.question: Which MG models use the 15S4C engine?
items.answer: The 15S4C is fitted to the MG3 (2011-2024) and the MG ZS (2017-present) in UK-market naturally aspirated 1.5-litre petrol form. It is not used in the MG HS, which uses a 1.5-litre turbo (15E4E). The 15S4C is also found in some Roewe and other SAIC-badged models outside the UK.
bullets: It is not used in the MG HS, which uses a 1.5-litre turbo (15E4E).

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned 15S4C?
items.answer: For most owners, a reconditioned 15S4C is the best choice because it addresses the known chain tensioner issue and includes a warranty. Used units are only advisable for very low-value cars (sub-£3,000) where the cost of a recon cannot be justified. Always request compression test results and chain history on any used unit.
bullets: Used units are only advisable for very low-value cars (sub-£3,000) where the cost of a recon cannot be justified.
Always request compression test results and chain history on any used unit.

items.question: How do I know if my MG has the 15S4C and not the 15S4E or 15S4F?
items.answer: The engine code is stamped on the front or side of the block and on the V5C registration document under “Engine number”. The 15S4C was fitted up to roughly 2018; later cars switched to 15S4E (2018-2023) and then 15S4F (2023+). Fitting the wrong revision may cause ECU mismatches - always match the exact suffix.
bullets: The 15S4C was fitted up to roughly 2018; later cars switched to 15S4E (2018-2023) and then 15S4F (2023+).
Fitting the wrong revision may cause ECU mismatches - always match the exact suffix.

items.question: Is the 15S4C a reliable engine overall?
items.answer: Yes, when properly maintained. The post-2015 tensioner improvement addressed the main weakness, and the engine is otherwise durable with good parts availability. Regular oil changes every 10,000 miles or annually are essential. Many owners report trouble‑free running beyond 100,000 miles with the later revisions.
